title: Finite injury and Post’s problem

based_on.title: Computability theory
based_on.pages: Version2024-02-25;§24.1,printed/PDF p.88,Theorem24.1; fresh-witness nonmembership corrected; effective stages expanded

based_on.title: Post’s problem
based_on.pages: Lecture slides2023-11-01,PDF pp.2–7; disjoint witness reservoirs, bounded attention and finite-injury verification

summary: Build two incomparable enumerable sets by effective priority stages and prove that both have degree strictly between computability and the halting problem.
abstract: An enumerable set can be undecidable without being powerful enough to decide the halting problem. Proving this requires more than the finite-extension construction: the positive answers must now be listed by an ordinary algorithm. We build two such sets together, asking each proposed oracle decision procedure to disagree with the other set at a private witness. A successful diagonalization protects the finitely many oracle answers it used. Higher-priority requirements may destroy that protection, so lower strategies restart with fresh witnesses. The construction itself uses only bounded computations and keeps every enumerated member permanently. Induction on priority proves that each requirement is injured only finitely often and eventually succeeds. The resulting enumerable sets cannot decide one another, which puts both degrees strictly between the computable degree and the halting degree and solves Post’s problem.
